chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazan ibn al-Khalil, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the rinsing (of the mouth) and the sniffing (of the water). He said: 'These two are not from the Ablution (Wudu); they are from the inside (of the body).'
ai.seo_question: Are rinsing the mouth and sniffing water considered part of Wudu or separate acts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory pillars of Wudu and the recommended acts of purification by clarifying that rinsing the mouth and sniffing water are not intrinsic components of the ritual ablution itself. Instead, he categorizes them as acts of cleansing the internal cavities (al-Jawf), highlighting a nuanced Shia jurisprudential view that separates external ritual validity from internal hygienic purity. This distinction underscores the importance of intention and the specific definition of 'Wudu' as a ritual act distinct from general bodily cleanliness.
